pdf_license: unknown (NIH author-manuscript deposit NIHMS2066430 in PubMed Central; no licence statement of any kind appears on the record)
notes: RETRIEVAL -- the strand brief supplied the DOI and PMCID. The PMC PDF at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11936488/pdf/nihms-2066430.pdf returns a 1,817-byte HTML interstitial ('Preparing to download ...') rather than the file, both with and without a Referer header, and the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint returns HTTP 404 for PMC11936488. The PDF was obtained instead from https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC11936488?pdf=render (15 pages, 949,654 bytes), which serves the same NIHMS author manuscript. LICENCE -- the brief's retrieval note anticipated two outcomes: 'author-accepted-manuscript' if the record is a standard author-manuscript deposit, or 'unknown' if the licence is unclear. What the record actually shows is both at once, and it is resolved here against the addendum rather than the brief. The PMC page identifies the deposit as an author manuscript (NIHMSID: NIHMS2066430; 'Trends Neurosci. Author manuscript; available in PMC: 2025 Oct 1') and carries a 'Copyright and License information' heading, but the section contains only affiliations, the PMC Copyright notice link, and identifiers -- no Creative Commons licence, no reuse grant, no licence URL. The Europe PMC REST record for DOI 10.1016/j.tins.2024.08.006 reports isOpenAccess 'N' and license null, and lists the publisher route as 'Subscription required'. So the deposit is free to read in PMC under the NIH Public Access Policy, which is a grant running to PMC, not to third parties -- structurally the same situation as arXiv's default non-exclusive licence, which the schema addendum resolves as 'unknown' with no committed PDF. Deny-by-default applied: pdf_license unknown, redistribution_ok false, no source.pdf committed. The publisher version of record is Elsevier and paywalled; it was not retrieved. EXTRACTION -- markitdown on the Europe PMC author manuscript. The layout carries a vertical 'Author Manuscript' watermark down the left margin of every page, which the converter emits as roughly 200 one-character lines per page interleaved with the body text; the running prose survives intact but is broken up by that noise, hence md_quality: rough. There are no tables in the article, so nothing tabular was lost. Figures 1-5 are not recoverable from the extraction, and the card makes no claim that depends on a figure. Reading was done against a whitespace-stripped working copy (lines of two characters or fewer removed) held outside the repository; source.md is the unmodified converter output. Retained as internal research notes under fair use, on the same footing as a paywalled paper's extraction.
